devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः ।
स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥ ६-१ ॥
englishScript:
Śrī Bhagavān Uvāca |
Anāśritaḥ Karma-phalaṁ Kāryaṁ Karma Karoti Yaḥ |
Sa Sannyāsī Ca Yogī Ca Na Niragnir Na Cākriyaḥ || 6-1 ||
translation: The Blessed Lord said: He who performs his obligatory duty without depending on the fruit of action is a renunciate and a yogi, not he who lights no sacrificial fire and performs no work.
explanationSentences: Paragraph 1 explores the foundational principles of the true definition of a yogi within the framework of Dhyana Yoga.
In this verse, krishna defines a true yogi as one who executes non-negotiable duty without outcome dependency.
Think of a small candle flame burning steadily inside a completely windless room (Yatha Deepo Nivatastho).
When there are zero drafts or air currents blowing through the room, the flame stands perfectly straight and still.
If a window opens and strong gusts blow in, the flame flickers wildly, casts unstable shadows, and risks going out.
Your mind and attention focus operate like that candle flame when you engage in deep study blocks or test solving.
When you shut out digital notifications, social noise, and grade anxiety, your mental flame burns with unshakeable stability.
Most students believe that controlling a restless mind requires impossible genetics or extreme physical torture.
However, first-principles deduction proves that mind control is a repeatable science mastered through practice (*Abhyasa*) and detachment (*Vairagya*).
Dhyana Yoga teaches you to elevate yourself by your own Self (*Uddhared Atmanatmanam*), making your mind your best friend.
Consider how a skilled rider trains a powerful wild stallion using patience, consistent reins, and gentle guidance.
When the horse bolts off the path, the rider doesn't panic or beat the animal; she simply pulls the reins and redirects it.
Whenever your attention drifts away from a complex problem, apply that exact mind-steering steering wheel technique.
Catch the distraction live at the very first step, drop self-blame, and gently guide your focus back to the target.
You gain total access to your prefrontal executive control, enabling zero-error calculation and deep problem-solving flow.
Notice how Krishna emphasizes moderate habits in eating, sleeping, work, and recreation (*Yuktahara-Vihara*).
Extreme sleep deprivation or over-eating creates heavy cognitive sluggishness that destroys your analytical speed.
Maintain a balanced daily routine so your brain receives optimal physical energy for peak intellectual performance.
Treat every practice problem as an exciting scientific experiment where mistakes provide valuable learning data.
If pre-test jitters occur, take three slow, deep belly breaths to stimulate your vagus nerve and restore logical reasoning.
Reframe your physical excitement as helpful performance energy mobilized by your body to help you execute fast.
Decouple your permanent human self-worth from temporary test marks so failure loses its power to intimidate you.
Develop an unquenchable obsession to uncover every hidden layer of logic behind formulas and concepts.
Remember that no good effort is ever wasted; past practice creates compound momentum that carries you forward.
Realize that true mastery is not passive daydreaming, but the active, systematic control of your internal focus.
Maintain your internal poise, execute with laser clarity, and let your genius shine.
This completes the deep exploration of verse 1, guiding you toward total emotional mastery and peace.
Stay focused, execute your daily routine with precision, and watch your problem-solving speed soar.
Burn like a windless flame, master your cognitive engine, and achieve unshakeable success.
Take complete ownership of your educational journey today, execute your work with joy, and realize your potential.
This marks the absolute completion of this profound lesson, unlocking supreme wisdom and steady cognitive power.

Manaḥ Saṁyamya Mac-citto Yukta Āsīta Mat-paraḥ || 6-14 ||
translation: Serene, fearless, firm in vows, controlling the mind, let him sit with mind absorbed in the Supreme, intent on Truth as the ultimate goal.
explanationSentences: Paragraph 14 explores the foundational principles of fearless serenity & absorption within the framework of Dhyana Yoga.
In this verse, cultivating fearless calm and absorbing attention completely in the core object.
Think of a small candle flame burning steadily inside a completely windless room (Yatha Deepo Nivatastho).
When there are zero drafts or air currents blowing through the room, the flame stands perfectly straight and still.
If a window opens and strong gusts blow in, the flame flickers wildly, casts unstable shadows, and risks going out.
Your mind and attention focus operate like that candle flame when you engage in deep study blocks or test solving.
When you shut out digital notifications, social noise, and grade anxiety, your mental flame burns with unshakeable stability.
Most students believe that controlling a restless mind requires impossible genetics or extreme physical torture.
However, first-principles deduction proves that mind control is a repeatable science mastered through practice (*Abhyasa*) and detachment (*Vairagya*).
Dhyana Yoga teaches you to elevate yourself by your own Self (*Uddhared Atmanatmanam*), making your mind your best friend.
Consider how a skilled rider trains a powerful wild stallion using patience, consistent reins, and gentle guidance.
When the horse bolts off the path, the rider doesn't panic or beat the animal; she simply pulls the reins and redirects it.
Whenever your attention drifts away from a complex problem, apply that exact mind-steering steering wheel technique.
Catch the distraction live at the very first step, drop self-blame, and gently guide your focus back to the target.
You gain total access to your prefrontal executive control, enabling zero-error calculation and deep problem-solving flow.
Notice how Krishna emphasizes moderate habits in eating, sleeping, work, and recreation (*Yuktahara-Vihara*).
Extreme sleep deprivation or over-eating creates heavy cognitive sluggishness that destroys your analytical speed.
Maintain a balanced daily routine so your brain receives optimal physical energy for peak intellectual performance.
Treat every practice problem as an exciting scientific experiment where mistakes provide valuable learning data.
If pre-test jitters occur, take three slow, deep belly breaths to stimulate your vagus nerve and restore logical reasoning.
Reframe your physical excitement as helpful performance energy mobilized by your body to help you execute fast.
Decouple your permanent human self-worth from temporary test marks so failure loses its power to intimidate you.
Develop an unquenchable obsession to uncover every hidden layer of logic behind formulas and concepts.
Remember that no good effort is ever wasted; past practice creates compound momentum that carries you forward.
Realize that true mastery is not passive daydreaming, but the active, systematic control of your internal focus.
Maintain your internal poise, execute with laser clarity, and let your genius shine.
This completes the deep exploration of verse 14, guiding you toward total emotional mastery and peace.
Stay focused, execute your daily routine with precision, and watch your problem-solving speed soar.
Burn like a windless flame, master your cognitive engine, and achieve unshakeable success.
Take complete ownership of your educational journey today, execute your work with joy, and realize your potential.
This marks the absolute completion of this profound lesson, unlocking supreme wisdom and steady cognitive power.
